theories.name: Framing
activationCriteria: A public text defines the issue, attributes cause, evaluates it, or recommends a treatment.
observableSignals: coded announcement, media, and community frames
frame share by language, channel, and day
theories.parameterization: Use deterministic text labels and bounded frame-strength assumptions; do not convert labels directly into risk coefficients.
forbiddenClaims: A frame label proves audience acceptance, causal effect, or population prevalence.
limitations: A frame label is not a causal estimate or a population prevalence estimate.

theories.name: Situational Crisis Communication Theory
activationCriteria: The case contains responsibility attribution and a publisher response or response alternative.
observableSignals: explanation, apology, correction, and compensation actions
theories.parameterization: Represent crisis type and history as bounded latent assumptions and the response as an explicit action vector; estimate no ZZZ-specific effect size.
forbiddenClaims: SCCT guarantees that a selected response will reduce risk in this game or version.
limitations: Current parameter weights are bounded research assumptions and are not historically calibrated effect sizes.

theories.name: Situational Theory of Problem Solving
activationCriteria: Public material contains observable problem, constraint, involvement, information-seeking, or information-sharing cues.
observableSignals: problem and constraint cues in public posts
seeking, selecting, forwarding, and sharing actions
theories.parameterization: Use latent appraisal ranges for synthetic representatives and keep public text codes separate from unobserved individual psychology.
forbiddenClaims: A public post reveals the psychological state of silent players or measures the full player population.
limitations: Public posts cannot identify silent players' latent appraisals without direct measurement.

theories.name: Collective behavior threshold model
activationCriteria: The simulation needs an explicit rule for when heterogeneous representatives begin public participation.
theories.parameterization: Run sensitivity ensembles over synthetic threshold distributions; do not infer a unique distribution from one aggregate event curve.
forbiddenClaims: A fitted synthetic threshold distribution represents the real player population.
limitations: Synthetic thresholds are mechanisms, not estimates of real population distributions.

theories.name: Social-Mediated Crisis Communication model
activationCriteria: The case spans official, third-party, social, or traditional media sources and observable seeking or sharing.
theories.parameterization: Encode channel roles, edge types, and bounded credibility assumptions; preserve platform sampling bias.
forbiddenClaims: Platform engagement or repost volume equals support rate or player-population prevalence.
limitations: Platform users and visible interactions do not represent the complete player population.

theories.name: Social Amplification of Risk Framework
activationCriteria: A signal moves through multiple individual, group, media, institutional, regional, or international layers.
theories.parameterization: Use bounded node and edge amplification assumptions across the 42-day graph and expose them to sensitivity analysis.
forbiddenClaims: Visibility amplification proves objective harm, true probability, or a universal coefficient.
limitations: The framework supplies no universal numeric amplification coefficient.

theories.name: Spiral of Silence
activationCriteria: The scenario explicitly separates private stance from public expression and labels both as synthetic latent variables.
observableSignals: public expression and opinion-climate proxies only
theories.parameterization: Keep private stance and expression propensity separate and use wide synthetic ranges when no survey measurement exists.
forbiddenClaims: Public voice reveals the private majority, silent share, or country-level opinion.
limitations: Public data cannot identify the opinions or size of silent groups.

theories.name: Relative deprivation
activationCriteria: The case contains an explicit comparison standard plus perceived unfairness, anger, or resentment.
theories.parameterization: Enable only for explicit reward, compensation, ownership, or differential-treatment comparisons; keep individual and group levels separate.
forbiddenClaims: General negative sentiment is sufficient evidence of relative deprivation.
limitations: The presence of comparison language does not establish deprivation as the sole cause of a response.

theories.name: Stakeholder salience
activationCriteria: A publisher decision layer must prioritize attention or response resources among stakeholder claims.
theories.parameterization: Use only in the publisher prioritization layer and keep the three perceived attributes separate.
forbiddenClaims: High volume proves legitimacy, correctness, or moral priority.
limitations: Influence or volume does not make a claim more correct or legitimate.

theories.name: Logic of connective action
activationCriteria: Evidence shows sustained decentralized coordination such as petitions, boycotts, or coordinated content reuse.
theories.parameterization: Enable graph coordination mode only when evidence exceeds ordinary short-lived complaint activity.
forbiddenClaims: A viral post or short complaint wave automatically constitutes connective action.
limitations: Public platform activity is an observed proxy and does not represent the full player population.

theories.name: Image Repair Discourse
activationCriteria: The case contains an official response statement that needs sentence-level strategy coding.
observableSignals: official statement sentences and response timing
theories.parameterization: Use as a response-action ontology alongside SCCT, not as a separate numerical propagation model.
forbiddenClaims: Selecting an image-repair category guarantees response effectiveness.
limitations: Response classification alone does not establish effectiveness.
